title: The 14-Day Inbox Warm-Up Checklist: One Brick a Day Before You Send
description: The warm-up checklist from the reel: what to do on day 1, day 3, day 7 and day 14, and how to ramp up after so new inboxes stay out of spam.
lead: This is the full warm-up checklist from the reel. A new inbox needs 14 days of steady warm-up before cold email goes out. Here's what to do each day, how to tell it's working, and how to ramp up after day 14.
insider: Every client inbox we run gets its full warm-up before a single cold email goes out, and warm-up never turns off. That steady base is how one client sent **236,545 emails in one quarter with a 3.69% reply rate**. The checklist is the easy part. Buying the domains, watching inbox health daily and swapping tired inboxes is what we do for clients.

blocks.text: Why a new inbox can't send on day one

A brand-new inbox has no history. Inbox providers don't know if it's a real person or a spammer. If it suddenly sends dozens of emails to strangers, it looks like a spammer, and your emails start going to spam.

[Google's sender guidelines](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/81126) say it plainly: start with a low sending volume and increase it slowly over time, and avoid sudden volume spikes if you don't have a history of sending. Warm-up builds that history.

**What warm-up is:** a tool sends and receives normal-looking emails between your inbox and a network of other real inboxes. They get opened, replied to and moved out of spam. Over time, providers learn your inbox is real. Tools like [Instantly](https://instantly.ai/email-warmup) and [Smartlead](https://www.smartlead.ai) do it automatically.

items: Use a separate sending domain, never your main business domain.
Add SPF, DKIM and DMARC on the domain. Our [DNS records guide](/blog/dns-records-for-cold-email.html) has the values.
Fill in the inbox profile: real first and last name and a profile photo.
Point the sending domain to your real website.
Connect the inbox to your sending tool and turn warm-up on.

blocks.label: Week one feels slow
blocks.text: Nothing exciting happens in week one. That's the point. Every steady day is a brick that holds up the next one.
After day 14: ramp up, don't jump

Day 14 is when you can start, not when you go full speed. [Instantly's 2026 benchmark report](https://instantly.ai/cold-email-benchmark-report-2026) recommends starting at **5 to 10 emails a day**, then building up over **4 to 6 weeks**.

head: Week
Cold emails per inbox per day
Warm-up

items: Weeks 1 and 2: warm-up only. **0 cold emails**.
Week 3: 10 inboxes × 10 = **100 cold emails a day**.
At 300 a day for 20 working days, that's **6,000 emails a month**, built on a base that holds.

blocks.text: How to tell the wall is holding

items: Warm-up emails land in the main inbox, not spam or promotions
Your tool's warm-up health score is high and steady
Bounce rate stays under 2% once you start (Instantly's guidance)
Google Postmaster Tools spam rate stays under 0.3% (Google's limit)
Replies come in, not just silence

blocks.label: AI prompt: plan your warm-up calendar
blocks.text:
I'm setting up [number] new sending inboxes on [number] domains, starting on [date].
My goal is [number] cold emails a day.

Make me a day-by-day calendar: 14 days of warm-up only, then a ramp of 10, 20 and 30 cold emails per inbox per day by week. Show the total emails per day for each week, and the date I reach my goal. If my inboxes can't reach the goal at 30 per inbox, tell me how many more inboxes I need.

blocks.label: Bottom line
blocks.text: Fourteen days of patience protects months of sending. Lay one brick a day, then build slowly.

faq.q: Can I send a few cold emails during warm-up?
faq.a: We don't recommend it. Give the inbox the full 14 days first, then start at about 10 a day.

faq.q: Do I need to turn warm-up off once I start sending?
faq.a: No. Keep it on, always. It keeps steady, healthy activity on the inbox.
It's enough to start slowly. Instantly recommends building to full volume over 4 to 6 weeks, so keep ramping after day 14.
